records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 [roadway] [roadway] 2 and unit 2 (raul) [roadway] [roadway] 2. unit 1 struck unit 2 with its front driver side bumper and continued nb on broadway fleeing the scene of the accident. when unit 2 was struck, [roadway] 2. garland fd a4 responded to the scene and advised raul had sustained a broken [medical facility] in dallas. it should be noted raul appeared to be heavily intoxicated. reference garland pd report #2025r021626. witness: bryan lundell (214) 801-9698. after investigation, unit 1 was identified with the assistance of flock cameras to the south of the crash, along with video evidence obtained from a business facing the roadway where the crash occurred. in the video, raul was observed crossing the roadway eastbound from a nearby parking lot. as raul was nearly across the #2 [roadway], within the 5200 and 5300 block, he was struck by the front right corner of unit 1. unit 1 was observed briefly stopping north of raul, before leaving the scene without any occupant attempting to render aid or provide their information. investigators located unit 1 and found damage to the front right corner, namely a lower-right fog light pushed out of it's housing and a missing reflector above the front-right tire, consistent with the video of the crash. investigators utilized cell phone records to establish probable cause to believe the driver of the vehicle at the time of the crash, was the registered owner, cahnce gray. a warrant was issued for his arrest for failure to stop and render aid- crash involving serious bodily injury. investigators spoke to raul, who had extensive injuries to his left leg including (4) broken toes.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 1307 hours, i, officer nelson #133, was dispatched to an auto pedestrian accident at [roadway] (wal-mart) in weatherford, tx. dispatch advised a shopping cart with 2 kids was struck by a vehicle. i arrived on scene at 1309 hours and observed a red jeep wrangler, txlp [identifier], in the pedestrian cross walk area of the parking lot facing south at the pharmacy entrance to the store. i observed a shopping cart on its left side at the front of the jeep and facing the store front. i observed two parents, skylah maxwell (w/f [date]) and cooper maxwell (w/m [date]), holding two small children, identified as casen maxwell (w/m [date]) and hudson maxwell (w/m [date]), that were crying. i quickly checked the children and did not observe any major injuries. i advised them to remain in the vestibule of the store until ems arrived on scene. i located the driver of the jeep, dorothy mitchell unit 1 (w/f [date] ph# [phone]) standing next to the jeep. i spoke with dorothy, who was visually upset and emotional. dorothy advised she turned the corner in the jeep and did not see the cart being pushed in front her. i believe the age of dorothy and the inability to react and be conscious of her surroundings are a contributing factor and needs to be looked at. dorothy stated to [roadway], she might as well be dead. ems arrived on scene and assessed the injuries to casen and hudson. the injuries appeared to be minor. hudson had red marks on his right hip. casen had red mark on back from buggy (left upper spine) and mid stomach from seat belt of buggy. casen was sitting in the buggy seat with the lap belt and hudson was sitting in the large basket portion of the buggy. i talked with skylah and cooper and they advised they were walking out of the store and cooper was pushing the buggy. skylah was walking on the right side of cooper. the jeep struck the buggy on the front left corner with its front bumper, turning the buggy sideways and tipping it over. skylah and cooper refused further assistance from ems because of only minor injuries. i advised they keep an eye on the children and take them in if any records.public_safe_text: on [date] at approximately 1307 hours, i, officer nelson #133, was dispatched to an auto pedestrian accident at [roadway] (wal-mart) in weatherford, tx. dispatch advised a shopping cart with 2 kids was struck by a vehicle. i arrived on scene at 1309 hours and observed a red jeep wrangler, txlp [identifier], in the pedestrian cross walk area of the parking lot facing south at the pharmacy entrance to the store. i observed a shopping cart on its left side at the front of the jeep and facing the store front. i observed two parents, skylah maxwell (w/f [date]) and cooper maxwell (w/m [date]), holding two small children, identified as casen maxwell (w/m [date]) and hudson maxwell (w/m [date]), that were crying. i quickly checked the children and did not observe any major injuries. i advised them to remain in the vestibule of the store until ems arrived on scene. i located the driver of the jeep, dorothy mitchell unit 1 (w/f [date] ph# [phone]) standing next to the jeep. i spoke with dorothy, who was visually upset and emotional. dorothy advised she turned the corner in the jeep and did not see the cart being pushed in front her. i believe the age of dorothy and the inability to react and be conscious of her surroundings are a contributing factor and needs to be looked at. dorothy stated to [roadway], she might as well be dead. ems arrived on scene and assessed the injuries to casen and hudson. the injuries appeared to be minor. hudson had red marks on his right hip. casen had red mark on back from buggy (left upper spine) and mid stomach from seat belt of buggy. casen was sitting in the buggy seat with the lap belt and hudson was sitting in the large basket portion of the buggy. i talked with skylah and cooper and they advised they were walking out of the store and cooper was pushing the buggy. skylah was walking on the right side of cooper. the jeep struck the buggy on the front left corner with its front bumper, turning the buggy sideways and tipping it over. skylah and cooper refused further assistance from ems because of only minor injuries. i advised they keep an eye on the children and take them in if any other symptoms of further injuries appear. skylah and cooper stated they understood. both skylah, cooper and mitchell were provided my card with cfs#. cooper advised he got angry and began striking the passenger window of the jeep multiple times, causing injury to his left hand. cooper said he then walked away to cool off. no observed damage to the window while units were on scene and mitchell never advised of any damage. wal-mart ap advised they would burn video and advised when a copy is ready.

records.deidentified_narrative: while conducting uniformed patrol, police responded to a call regarding an information report. the call notes stated that sb1 had been struck by a motor vehicle four days ago, [medical facility] twice for a slipped disc. upon arrival at the listed location, i made contact with sb1, an employee at the location. sb1 reported that approximately four days prior, on december 10th, 2025, she was struck by a motor vehicle while in the parking lot. sb1 stated that she had gone to the parking lot to smoke a cigarette and, while returning inside the building, was struck when a white midsized suv backed into her, impacting her left hip. sb1 stated that the vehicle was traveling at approximately five miles per hour at the time of impact. sb1 reported that after being struck, she slapped the passenger-side window of the vehicle and told the driver, you hit me, or words to that effect, in an effort to confront him. sb1 stated that the driver responded by saying, theres no parking here, after being confronted. sb1 then reported that she stormed off and returned inside the building. i found it noteworthy that sb1 was able to immediately walk back into the building without apparent difficulty following the incident. sb1 admitted that she did not attempt to identify the driver or obtain the vehicles license plate information. sb1 stated that she did not contact emergency services following the incident [medical facility]. sb1 denied the need for ems. sb1 reported experiencing pain on the left side of her leg and stated that she had been treating the pain with advil, tylenol, ice, and heat compressions. sb1 denied having any visible injuries as a result of the incident. i did not observe any visible signs of injury to sb1 at the time of contact. based on my observations and sb1s statements, it is my opinion that sb1 did not appear to be in need of medical attention at the time of this report. when asked why there was a delay in reporting the incident, sb1 stated that she did not know what to do after the event occurred. sb1 reported that she needed a report so her company could release surveillance footage of the vehicle involved in the incident. sb1 was provided with a [case id] the incident. dmea.
